title: R' Tavi
author: Aharon Hyman

paragraphs: He was a Babylonian, and there he was called only Tavi, as in [Temurah 34a:3-5](https://www.sefaria.org/Temurah.34a.3-5): Tavi posed a contradiction to Rav Nachman — Tavi said to Rav Nachman, “You have resolved the nazirite [contradiction]” — Rav Nachman was silent — Rav Nachman asked Tavi, “Have you heard anything about this?” Tavi replied: “Thus said Rav Sheshet,” etc. Likewise he spoke in Rav Chisda’s name in Jerusalem Talmud Shabbat 3:7 and Sukkah, chapter 3, end of halakhah 1.

According to Hyman, he afterward went up to the Land of Israel and was the student of R' Yoshiyah (II), as in [Berakhot 15b](https://www.sefaria.org/Berakhot.15b.20-21) and [63a](https://www.sefaria.org/Berakhot.63a.22) and [Yoma 65b](https://www.sefaria.org/Yoma.65b.1), where Tavi speaks in the name of R' Yoshiyah. In Jerusalem Talmud Terumot 2:1 (folio 7a in Hyman’s citation): R' Tavi in the name of R' Yoshiyah, designated בי ר׳ ינאי; and Shekalim, beginning of chapter 1: R' Tavi, R' Yoshiyah in the name of Kahana.

Likewise we find in the Jerusalem Talmud, Terumot, chapter 8, end of halakhah 3; Sukkah, beginning of chapter 2; and Sotah, chapter 3, end of halakhah 1, that he spoke in Rav’s name. In Shabbat, end of chapter 19: R' Tavai in the name of Shmuel; and Yevamot 8:1 reads R' Tavi in the name of Shmuel.

Hyman cites Megillah 6a (compare [Megillah 6b:27](https://www.sefaria.org/Megillah.6b.27)): “R' Tavi said: The reason of R-Sh-B-G,” etc. Of those who speak in his name we find R' Chizkiyah: Terumot, chapter 8, end of halakhah 3.[^6]
R' Yose in his name: Sukkah, beginning of chapter 3; Sotah, chapter 3, end of halakhah 1.
We also find R' Avudmi, the daughter’s son of R' Tavi: Sanhedrin 6:5.

The supplied Hebrew has Temurah. Hyman’s printed notice (vol. II, p. 521) reads Terumot, and the corresponding report is in Jerusalem Talmud Terumot 2:1. The Hebrew of the Guggenheimer edition places Tavi and Yoshiyah next to one another without Hyman’s “in the name of.” Guggenheimer translates בי ר׳ ינאי as “the son of Rabbi Yannai.” The designation is left in Hebrew because the relationship remains open.

Jerusalem Talmud Shabbat 3:7 explicitly names Rav Chisda. At the beginning of Sukkah chapter 3, the consulted edition has a Tavi chain in the name of Rav. Hyman’s citation of Megillah 6a is retained; the quoted rationale is on 6b in the consulted edition. Jerusalem Talmud Sanhedrin 6:5 names Abdomai as the son of Tavi’s daughter.

Terumot 8:3 names Chizkiyah, Tavi, and Rav in that order. Shabbat chapter 19 and Yevamot 8:1 give the respective forms Tavai and Tavi in the name of Shmuel. The reports Hyman cites in Sotah and his attribution to Rav at the beginning of Sukkah chapter 2 remain unconfirmed in the passages consulted.

In Temurah, Rav Nachman answers Tavi’s first difficulty about a nazirite. Tavi presses a second question and reports Rav Sheshet’s answer. In Megillah, Tavi explains why it is preferable to place the celebrations of the two redemptions, Purim and Passover, close together.
